articles.title: How to Bypass Rust's Orphan Rule
articles.summary: Rust's Orphan Rule is a well-known limitation that prevents a type from implementing a trait from another third-party crate, even if the trait is defined in the same crate. This rule is enforced by Rust to prevent global conflicts and maintain coherence in the ecosystem. By design, the rule leaves a wide door open, allowing developers to make a third-party type implement a trait from another third-party crate. However, this approach can become awkward when dealing with complex projects that require multiple libraries to work together.
